# Test: apx release prepare --audience records the audience in the manifest

mkdir app-repo
cd app-repo
exec git init
exec git config user.name 'Test User'
exec git config user.email 'test@example.com'
exec apx init app --org=myorg --repo=app-repo --non-interactive internal/apis/proto/payments/ledger/v1
exec git add .
exec git commit -m 'Add ledger API'

# Without the flag the manifest has no audience key
exec apx release prepare proto/payments/ledger/v1 --version=v1.0.0 --canonical-repo=github.com/myorg/apis
exists .apx-release.yaml
! grep 'audience' .apx-release.yaml

# With the flag the manifest carries the audience
exec apx release prepare proto/payments/ledger/v1 --version=v1.0.0 --canonical-repo=github.com/myorg/apis --audience internal
grep '^audience: internal$' .apx-release.yaml

exec apx release prepare proto/payments/ledger/v1 --version=v1.0.0 --canonical-repo=github.com/myorg/apis --audience public
grep '^audience: public$' .apx-release.yaml

# An unknown audience fails
! exec apx release prepare proto/payments/ledger/v1 --version=v1.0.0 --canonical-repo=github.com/myorg/apis --audience device
stderr 'invalid audience "device"'

# The finalize CI mode validates the flag too
! exec apx release finalize --api proto/payments/ledger/v1 --version v1.0.0 --audience device
stderr 'invalid audience "device"'
